pr_title: Ensure frontend is available if integrations fail to start - Part 1 of 2
pr_body:
Part 1 of 2.  

When integrations configured via the UI block startup or fail to start,
the webserver can remain offline which make it is impossible
to recover without manually changing files in
`.storage` since the UI is not available.

This change is the foundation that part 2 will build on
and enable a listener to start the webserver when the frontend
is finished loading.

Frontend Changes (https://github.com/home-assistant/frontend/pull/6068)

I think loading the frontend earlier is always a win. It will make the startup feel way faster to the user.

Things I can think off:
- Don't allow removing restored entities before complete startup
- Generated Lovelace, it can show the "you have no devices available" message, so we would have to catch that when we haven't complete startup and regenerate when startup is completed. But I also see it restoring entities slowly and finally showing just a limited amount of cards (I guess we regenerate Lovelace on connect, should move that to the started event, but only when not started yet)
- When you are on a panel on restart that is not loaded on frontend start it will not show after startup
- Probably some more stuff that will not work until after a refresh

The rest behaves pretty well because we update the UI when something changes, so you will see the sidebar, config panel, integrations build-up slowly.
Too many conflicts, will resquash

~~Unable to serialize to JSON. Bad data found at $.result.state=RUNNING(<enum 'CoreState'>`~~

Fixed

Re Bram's earlier list. Restored entities are not written to the state machine until the start event. So that's not a problem. 

We're going to miss something and it is going to bite us. I think worst case we can always roll it back. 

We need to make sure that we do block any sync with external systems until we're fully started or else an external system will miss entities and thus throw them away. HomeKit, Alexa and Google are all controlled from within Home Assistant so we should be able to block syncing until we are started (I think we already are). However if an integration is connecting TO Home Assistant, it will miss things. How do we deal with that ? 

I guess we can tell those integrations to check for the `homeassistant_started` event. Because of race conditions, any integration waiting for Home Assistant to be started should refetch the config after the event subscription for `ha_started` is in place because it could have been fired while subscribing.

Incoming webhooks/cloudhooks could get premature updates, but I haven't found a case where I think thats an issue yet.

Maybe IFTTT could send a webhook for an integration not yet loaded.

Could have webhooks give a 503 if the started event has not yet fired. 

`git grep requires_auth = False`

Then again I'm not sure many things retry anyways so its not much different than losing the event now.
Maybe a config flag for `http` `fast_start` that can be set to `false`?

Integrations are either taking data in and representing it as events or states or integrations provide automations. Since our automation integrations don't start until the start event, I don't think that we have to worry about webhooks.

Waiting for a final sign off from @pvizeli to make sure that the Supervisor health check still works as intended or that we need it tweaking before we merge this. 

For frontend, I think that we should implement:
 - panel resolver, when it cannot find a panel, should check if Home Assistant is still starting, if so, it should show a spinner "Waiting for Home Assistant to start".
 - Generated Lovelace should probably just wait until started too. It will jump around too much otherwise?

> Waiting for a final sign off from @pvizeli to make sure that the Supervisor health check still works as intended or that we need it tweaking before we merge this.

It breaks the hole add-on flows. It's how we detect a running instance and not the health check but that needs to be also tweaked. I will look after my baby break into that topic (2 months).

EDIT: Don't get me wrong. I'm fine with this movement. It's just that I have too much work until my baby holiday. We can also freeze the Home Assistant Container/Supervisord release pipeline and move forward with the Core. But somethings like this are not just a small supervisor update, for that we need a longer test phase and I have really not the head for that now.
I'm wondering if we add `hassio` to Phase 1 it could allow us to avoid the need to make any supervisor changes.

Moved `hassio` to phase 1 as we aren't worried about `hassio` blocking startup.  I think this makes sense since we want the user to be able to access the addons as soon as possible as well.  They may want to use the ssh web ui to fix something that is breaking startup and have no other way to access the instance remotely.  


Created an integration that blocks startup for 301 seconds.  All the panels now work on reconnect when I'm on the supervisor panel and trigger a restart.

Looks like its a `connect()` check which will now happen much sooner and return from the checks sooner.   That seems to be OK though as the code after it was checking for db schema and pip installs to avoid declaring premature failure, which no longer block the connect()

I'm not sure if its actually ever an issue, but there is still a small race window where its possible that the frontend is finished loading before `hassio`, the `frontend` loaded event fires, the webserver starts, the reconnect happens, and `hassio` hasn't finished registering its endpoints.   It probably can't actually happen now, but if we ever refactor `hassio` to take longer to load than `frontend`, it could break having the panel immediately available on reconnect.

If we think this is a real risk, we could fire a `STARTING` event after all the phase1 integrations are loaded and wait for that to start the webserver.  It would likely be a few milliseconds later and it would mean adding another event.
It doesn't matter if the panel is registered after the frontend load, that will work fine, the problem is more for the add-ons and to check for a rollback I guess?

Rollback is definitely a hot spot here as moving forward its going to depend on behavior we want:

- If we want to rollback if the webserver fails to start, this is the behavior we would have with this PR as-is.  This gives the user the option of fixing whatever is now blocking startup from finishing on the new version OR they should still be able to access the supervisor UI and go back to the last snapshot.  **I'm not sure if there will be a snapshot for them to rollback to since we don't appear to create one for before update as it looks like the rollback functions by changing the docker image back to the old version.**   

- If we want to rollback if the Home Assistant start event isn't fired after 10m, we would need to modify `supervisor.homeassistant.HomeAssistant._block_till_run` to poll the core api and wait for the start event after the `connect()` check is successful.

## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->

If there is an issue setting up the camera integration, the HTTP server will fail to load and home assistant will be completely inaccessible.

## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.110 
- Last working Home Assistant Core release (if known): 0.109.6 
- Operating environment (Home Assistant/Supervised/Docker/venv): Docker
- Integration causing this issue: http + camera
- Link to integration documentation on our website: 

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
- platform: generic
  # Note that this camera is currently unplugged, but didn't cause any problems in 0.109.x
  still_image_url: http://192.168.1.96/snap.jpeg
  stream_source: rtsp://192.168.1.60:7447/5de6188051ec9659df33fsdceb6441b2_2
  name: G3 Flex
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt

```

## Additional information

There wouldn't be any errors visible to suggest the problem, I had to go through my integrations one by one to find the culprit. Instead, it would always be in the `starting` state and never complete. Removing the unavailable cameras fixes the issue.

The issue should be reproducible by setting up a generic camera pointing to a URL with a long timeout on it. 

There are similar issues at #35873 and #35888

Integrations can take a while to install dependencies so we can't cancel them sooner without risking breaking an integration that would actually startup if we gave it enough time. #36082 is more of a fail safe.

We already log when an integration is taking more than 10s to startup.

#36093 has a more substantive change where we made the webserver and frontend available very soon after startup.

I'm not saying they should be cancelled, just they the logging should be improved. There's a massive jump between 10 seconds and 30 minutes, with the user not knowing what's happening in between.

A log on a 1m loop with something like

``` 
Waiting for the following integrations to complete:
- [ ] camera
- [x] rest
- [x] spotify
```

For example would make debugging much better.
However the fix in #36093 would also go a long way in helping.

review_comments:
We also need `config` or else we don't have APIs to manage the config entries.

```suggestion
    "frontend",
    "config",
```
This is going to be a problem for anything spawned by an API interaction by the user while Home Assistant is starting up.
I'm thinking long running logbook api calls or history api calls could block startup for a few seconds.  Is there anything else that is a problem hot spot that I'm not thinking about?

Two things I can think of:
 - Triggering a script that takes X time
 - Starting a config flow for new integration that starts installation of a big requirements (like `zwave`)
I don't think that it would be a big problem, eventually all tasks should stop and no websocket API should start long running tasks
This seems to do a very similar thing as #36082. I think that we should keep it out of this PR as it's already impactful enough.

I'm concerned about taking it out as the user can now interact with the api/ui and trigger something in an integration that blocks for a long time like websocket did.  Taking it out might rehash #6973
We should use `asyncio.create_task` now. It's recommended from Python 3.7.
